Guidance & outlook: As can be seen from the last three quarters, the performance on the brand is improving, and this is quite encouraging as we move into the next quarter.
We expect this impact to also be short term in nature.
And in the long term, we remain quite positive about the business.
Growth & demand: Q1 FY '27 was our second consecutive quarter of strong performance with 15% revenue growth, best in the last eleven quarters and 32% adjusted EBITDA growth, best in the last fifteen quarters.
Our Q1 FY '27 revenue was INR 888 crores, up 15%, as I said.
I want to emphasize this was a really strong quarter for us: KFC SSSG growth, KFC EBITDA growth, 15% consolidated growth, which was the best in our 11 quarters.
Margins & costs: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA came in at INR75 crores, up 37% year-on-year and margin was 8.4%.
And while gross margin improved, as mentioned by Sanjay, the higher energy c ost, wage inflation impacted the overall restaurant EBITDA, which came in at 12%.
Irrespective of the brand, typically at a 3% to 5% SSSG, when you start comparing with the last year's number, it takes care of the inflation in terms of the wage cost and the other costs in the P&L.
Capex & expansion: On Pizza Hut, we have called out that we will be quite cautious in terms of store expansion.
And I'm calling out calendar year because that's how we operate with Yum! in terms of store expansion plans.
And until the expansion happens, it will be difficult to drive double -digit growth or 15% growth.
Balance sheet & cash: This, combined with improved dine -in and takeaway mix, better operating leverage meant that the restaurant EBITDA improved by 120 basis points over last year.
Sir, my question is that we are seeing some operating leverage in play with the numbers.
Having said that, because we were able to get efficiencies this year on various cost lines, that has helped us create leverage even at 3% to 5% SSSG.
Risks & challenges: And this is despite the challenges in terms of the pricing pressures which we faced on the energy cost, especially in the terms of gas cost.
If you could also give us some sense on where the ADS needs to be for us to come back to that about 18% - 20% restaurant level margins, because we have had 2.5 years of soft SSSG.
Last year, we delivered 11% growth and the SSSG was quite challenging.

guidance.t: And the focus in the near term would be to drive SSSG and not try to take the margin towards 18%.
